summary: Editor highlights fitted to the palette keep text and every syntax colour readable: in Compare's unified Diff and Split views, the text selection in the focused editor, Find's other and current matches and the added and removed changed-word tints are drawn in colours fitted per palette, so text, every syntax colour (keyword, identifier, type, function, field, string, number, comment) and the unified patch's hunk, added and removed colours reach 4.5:1 or more on each, sampled from the frames in Midnight, Daylight, Porcelain and Omarchy Tokyo Night at interface 13 pt with code 12 pt and in Midnight with code 18 pt, while the base draws the selection and Find on the palette's selected and the word tints on origin's strong tint; the inspector's selected row, which keeps selected, is identical in both builds
limitations: Linux X11 under XWayland at scale factor 1 only, on display :0 with Mutter RemoteDesktop input; windows 1200x800 (code 12 pt) and 1700x900 (code 18 pt); four palettes, one Omarchy theme (Tokyo Night, seeded into each launch's HOME from the app's own test fixture). The caret of the focused editor (selection frames) and of the Find field (Find frames) blinks every 500 ms, so a re-check can differ at the caret alone. Compare's editors draw no active line, so the panel colour the fitting also keeps highlights apart from is sampled from the Find bar and the split headers, which the palette's panel fills, not from an editor line. The glyph analyses report the peak ink colour of each box: anti-aliasing can keep thin strokes (a single 'w', 's' or '/') from showing their colour unblended, so those peaks are lower bounds of the colour drawn. The distinctness measure (ΔEOK, Euclidean distance in OKLab) has no analysis kind: the fill analyses record each highlight's and each line's colour, and ΔEOK is computed from those recorded colours. Find's current match on the unified patch carries only text (context line 10) and its other match only the added colour; the hunk and removed colours on the selection are shown in unified-selection. macOS, native Wayland, fractional scales, the Before/After source tabs, the editor's active line and the other built-in and Omarchy palettes are not covered

fixture.name: editor-highlights-keep-syntax-readable
fixture.description: two commits on main: the first adds src/strip.rs, a short Rust file; the second replaces its lines 11 and 12 (let v: Grid = cut(s.pad, "off", 7); // down and return v;) with let mut w: Span = fit(s.gap, "on", 42); // ups and w, so the removed and added lines carry word-level changes in every syntax role (keyword, identifier, type, function, field, string, number and comment), and the added line repeats context line 10 up to its comment, which the Find query matches twice
